call_points.text: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at ₹1,400-1,500 Cr, EBITDA at ₹525-575 Cr
Core crane rental margin fell to 47% YoY due to ECL provisions and strategic mix shift
Gross debt-to-equity at 0.54x, guided to reach 0.72x by FY27 end
GCC DSO at 201 days due to regional disruptions, but collections improving in July
Crane rental business is expected to grow another 30% year-on-year.
Deferred KSA capex of ₹123 crores with 57 cranes will be spent this financial year.
Order book of ₹1,053 crores as of May 14 is fully executable in FY27.
Inquiry pipeline has expanded to almost ₹4,000 crores.
Blended EBITDA margin is falling as revenue shifts to the asset-light E&C business, which has ROCE of about 70%.
50% of clients supply fuel free; for the rest, the company is in advanced talks on a price increase as diesel rises.
Net debt was ₹612 crores at March 2026 with net debt-to-equity of 0.47x; leverage will rise a little with capex.
Average cost of borrowing was stable at 8.12% per annum.
Shipping congestion into Saudi Arabia and Qatar could postpone capex; Jeddah is also congested and rerouting is costly.
Management declined to give a blended EBITDA margin target, saying each business unit runs its own P&L.
Wind E&C delivered 2 GW of the country's 6 GW of wind capacity added in FY26.
Secured opening order book for FY27 stands at ₹1,053 Cr as on 14th May 2026.
Deferred ₹123 Cr of KSA capex from FY26 to FY27.

Hence, the Department's appeal stood dismissed. Basis the above favorable judgement for FY 2008-09 from High Court , refund Letter was submitted to Nodal officer on 03 Sep 2025. In case of assesment for FY 2010-11 final hearing is scheduled on 15th June 2026, other assessments from FY 2011-12 to FY 2017-18, awaiting for hearing from department before the first Appellate Authority. To best of our knowledge & information Maharashtra Sales department didn't file an appeal in next available forum & therefore it does not have any impact on financial performance of the company.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Input Tax Credit (ITC) claimed in GSTR-3B/GSTR-9 for the financial year 2017-18 exceeds the amount confirmed in GSTR-2A or 8A of GSTR-9.
tax_litigation.status: As per the provisions of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) law, ITC can only be claimed to the extent reflected in GSTR-2A/8A. Therefore, the excess ITC claimed in GSTR-3B/9 is not eligible for set-off, leading to its disallowance in the assessment. An appeal was filed against the demand notice with the Maharashtra GST Department on 22nd July 2022. Company believes that they have a strong merit in the case & will ger favorable order.
